audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows were inverted against both the packet chart and the already-audited mirror: Level 1 and Level 6 were given to Neeko, Level 2 was Skill, and 2+ items was Gragas.
audit.why: The mirror set Skill / Gragas / ... / Gragas / ... / Skill on those rows and the packet chart agrees. My own why-text also already agreed: whys[0] calls Level 1 'a genuine coin-flip', whys[4] says his knockback interrupts Pop Blossom so 6 does not convert, whys[6] says late 'evens out'. Only the side tokens were stale.
audit.corrected: Row 0 Neeko -> Skill (7/10 -> 5/10), row 1 Skill -> Gragas, row 4 Neeko -> Gragas (7/10 -> 4/10), row 6 Gragas -> Skill (4/10 -> 5/10). One atomic group, every full/content pair proposed together.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as Neeko's spike while the text on the same page explains why it isn't one.
audit.why: Explosive Cask knocks back and Body Slam stuns; either one lands on the Pop Blossom preparation and the ult is gone. That is the opposite of a power spike for Neeko in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Row 4 moved to Gragas and the spike text left describing his threat window, which it already did correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer refers to a Gragas 'Q-pool' five times — sitting in it, last-hitting in it, out-sustaining with it. Gragas has no pool. Barrel Roll is a cask that rolls to a location and explodes, and his sustain is Happy Hour (P), which heals him when he uses a skill.
audit.why: Riot's text for Q describes a rolling cask with a 4-second fuse and a slow; nothing about a pool or standing in it. A player told to 'deny his Q-pool last-hits' is being told to play around an ability that does not exist, and the real sustain lever — casting anything at all triggers Happy Hour — goes untaught.
audit.corrected: whys[1], whys[3], spikes[0].text, early, late and wants.foe[1] now name Happy Hour as the sustain and Barrel Roll as a cask.

audit.whatIsWrong: Drunken Rage's auto-attack reset was never named as the burst tell.
audit.why: _missing flags autoreset-burst-tell for this matchup. Riot's text: he samples his brew for 1 second, then his next basic attack deals magic damage in an area and he takes reduced damage. The 1-second drink is a visible wind-up — that is the cue to step back, not the moment he walks at you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Body Slam is called 'the clock this lane runs on' with no number anywhere on the page.
audit.why: It is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12s — a long window at rank 1 and the single thing that decides whether a step-up is free. The mirror recorded the same correction from Gragas's side.
audit.corrected: 14s at rank 1 written into dosFull[0].d and early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal appears only in the itemization report line and never in the prose that explains why the lane is unwinnable in a brawl.
audit.why: _missing flags needs-antiheal. Happy Hour turns every one of his casts into healing, so extended trades are decided by whether Grievous Wounds is on the board.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds timing written into late.

edits.before: His E body-slam comes online and dodges your Tangle-Barbs while closing to chunk you, and his Q-pool out-sustains your single-target poke.
edits.after: Body Slam comes online and dodges your Tangle-Barbs while closing to chunk you, and Happy Hour heals him back every time he casts a spell.

edits.before: He can E-dash through your telegraphed E and his W damage-reduction blunts any Q poke you do land — you have no all-in without ult.
edits.after: He dashes through your telegraphed E, and the one-second Drunken Rage drink is the tell that an empowered auto and damage reduction land next.

edits.before: Pre-6 you can't punish a sustaining Gragas: his Q-pool heals your pokes off and his dash dodges every root you throw.
edits.after: Pre-6 you can't punish a sustaining Gragas: Happy Hour heals your pokes off on every cast and Body Slam dodges the roots you throw.

edits.before: Both griefless and rangeless at 1 — you only have single-target Q, so just shove and deny his Q-pool last-hits.
edits.after: Both rangeless at Level 1 — you only have single-target Q, so shove the wave and deny him comfortable last-hits.

edits.before: Level 1 is a wash — you only have single-target Q and he just wants to last-hit in his Q-pool, so shove the wave and deny him free sustain rather than walking up. The lane tilts the moment he has E: his body-slam dash both dodges your Tangle-Barbs (E) and closes the gap to chunk you, and his Q-pool out-sustains your pokes. Don't throw E as your opener — he'll just dash through it; hold it as a peel/disengage tool and farm with the tip of Q.
edits.after: Level 1 is a wash — you only have single-target Q and he just wants free last-hits, so shove the wave and deny him the Happy Hour sustain rather than walking up. The lane tilts the moment he has E: Body Slam both dodges your Tangle-Barbs (E) and closes the gap to chunk you, and it is only down 14s at rank 1. Don't throw E as your opener — he'll dash through it; hold it as a peel and disengage tool and farm with the tip of Q.

edits.before: Stop trying to win the 1v1 — you won't out-brawl a Gragas who builds tank-AP and reduces your burst with W. Your value is shoving with Q and leaving: roam, gank, and be the teamfight bomb who Pop Blossoms a clustered enemy. Late, he's just one knockback and you're an AoE pick threat, so the lane evens out on the map even though he beat you in the dirt. Convert your 6-and-first-item roam timings into kills elsewhere instead of forcing a losing lane.
edits.after: Stop trying to win the 1v1 — Drunken Rage cuts your burst and Happy Hour heals it back, so buy Grievous Wounds before you plan any extended trade. Your value is shoving with Q and leaving: roam, gank, and be the teamfight bomb who Pop Blossoms a clustered enemy. Late, he's one knockback and you're an AoE pick threat, so the lane evens out on the map even though he beat you in the dirt. Convert your roam timings into kills elsewhere instead of forcing a losing lane.

edits.before: Sit in his Q-pool to out-sustain your Q pokes while his W eats your burst
edits.after: Heal off your Q pokes with Happy Hour every cast while Drunken Rage eats the burst

edits.before: His engage and his escape in one button — punish the cooldown hard. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Body Slam is his engage and his escape in one button, 14s at rank 1 — bait it, count it, then go.

notes: Two things left alone deliberately. First, spikes[1].text and wants.foe[2] both build advice around 'E-flash': Flash-buffering a dash is not in Riot's description and the kit's needsResearch is empty, so I did not assert or remove it — recorded as unverified. Second, the difficulty is 7/10 TRICKY with a 33.33% win rate over 15 games and the chart now reads Gragas on five of seven rows; TRICKY may be understating it, but diff, diffRating, tone and breakdown.difficulty all have to move together and the mirror deliberately left that call to the user, so I did too.
